summary: Anton Boller was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He joined the Austrian Academy of Sciences as a corresponding member in 1848 and served at the University of Vienna from 1845, becoming professor of comparative linguistics and Sanskrit in 1855.

Anton Eduard Wollheim da Fonseca specialized in Indology and linguistics. After earning his Dr. phil. at Humboldt University of Berlin (circa 1828–1831), he lectured there on Oriental and modern Western languages (1849–1852) and held a post at the Royal Danish Library.

Anton Schiefner studied law at Saint Petersburg State University and Oriental studies at Humboldt University of Berlin. Active in Tibetology, linguistics, and Indology, he held posts at Saint Petersburg First Gymnasium, the Roman Catholic Theological Academy, and the Russian Academy of Sciences.
Anton Westermann studied at Leipzig University from 1825 to 1830. He subsequently served as co-director at Leipzig University from 1830 to 1865, where he taught Friedrich Max Müller.

Antonello Palumbo is a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He held posts at SOAS University of London, attested in 2005 and 2010, where he taught Brian J. Nichols and Aristotle C. Dy.

Antonino Forte worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He held professorships at the Hōbōgirin Institute, the Italian School of East Asian Studies, the Istituto Italiano di Cultura's Sezione di Studi Orientali, and the University of Naples "L'Orientale," also serving at EFEO.

Antonio Gargano worked in Indology and other fields. He held a position as professor at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (attested 1966) and served as a curator and editor for Serie Orientale Roma (attested 1988).

Antonio T. de Nicolás worked in Indology and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Fordham University (circa 1964–1968) and served as a professor of philosophy at Stony Brook University from circa 1969 to 1996, later becoming professor emeritus.

Antonio Terrone specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Leiden University in 2010 under Tilmann Vetter and Barend J. ter Haar, and later served as scholar in residence at the Buddhist Digital Resource Center.

Anuj Misra works in Indology and history/archaeology. Having studied under Clemency Montelle and Kim Plofker, he holds a post as an external researcher at the University of Copenhagen (attested 2026).

Anukul Chandra Banerjee was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya and earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta. He served as assistant lecturer in Pali at Calcutta (attested 1943) and director of the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology.

Archibald Edward Gough studied under Monier Monier-Williams before serving as Anglo-Sanskrit Professor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1868–1878). In Indology and philosophy, he later worked as Professor of Philosophy at Presidency College, Kolkata, and Principal of Aliah University (both ~1881–1895).
Arghyadip Mondal works in Buddhist studies, computational fields, and Indology. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD researcher and faculty member at Ghent University.
Ariane Macdonald is a Tibetology scholar who studied under Rolf Alfred Stein. She held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, where she taught Amy Heller and Yoshiro Imaeda.

Arindam Chakrabarti earned his DPhil at the University of Oxford and works in philosophy and Indology. He held professorships at the University of Delhi and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, later holding the Mattoo Endowed Chair at Stony Brook University (attested 2026).
Arinde L. Jonker is an Indology scholar who completed a Research MA at Leiden University (attested 2018), where she studied under Jonathan A. Silk and MA supervisor Peter Bisschop.
Aristotle C. Dy specializes in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Antonello Palumbo (attested 2013).
Aritri Dutta works in Tibetology and religious studies. Attested in 2026, she is an external PhD candidate at Leiden University studying under doctoral supervisor Henk Blezer.

Arjo Vanderjagt studied at Franklin Academy, Prattsburgh Central School, and the University of Groningen (1971–1981). Working in philosophy and history/archaeology, he held academic posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1976–1979), Utrecht University (2007), and the University of Groningen (1994–2009).

Arlo Griffiths studied at Harvard and earned his PhD at Leiden under Henk Bodewitz. Specializing in Indology and linguistics, he held posts at Leiden, the University of Groningen, the Kern Institute, and became a professor at EFEO in 2008.
